explainer: The single best AI-bubble bellwether is the rental price of an installed Nvidia GPU, measured in dollars per GPU-hour, and specifically the H100: it is the daily marginal clearing price for AI compute, it is published by independent indexes (Silicon Data's SDH100RT, SemiAnalysis's one-year contract index), and a CME futures contract on it is pending: the CFTC extended its review to November 9, 2026, so a forward curve is coming but not yet listed. Right now it is saying the opposite of discounting: the Silicon Data index sits at $2.75/hr (Sep 30), a new high, one-year contract rates rose about 40% from $1.70 to $2.35 between October 2025 and March 2026, spot has run at roughly twice contract, and a four-year-old chip is renting for more than it did a year ago while CoreWeave says it has contracted 2020-vintage GPUs out to 2029 at full price. Pair it with three things: neocloud credit spreads (CoreWeave's July loan cleared at SOFR+550 for a 10.44% yield with maintenance covenants, and its CDS implies roughly a coin-flip default probability), which is the financing leg and the one signal already flashing red; server DRAM and HBM contract-price momentum (+13-18% QoQ in 3Q26 after +93-98% in 1Q26, with 4Q26 guided to only +3-8%), because memory is the first physical input that will roll over; and hyperscaler backlog growth versus capex growth (Microsoft commercial RPO +84%, Oracle RPO +363%, roughly $2.4 trillion of committed cloud backlog against about $1 trillion of 2026 capex), because the bubble only deflates if the buyers stop signing. Over the next one to two quarters watch Nvidia's August 26 print for gross margin and customer concentration (three direct customers were already 54% of revenue), the shape of the CME H100/B200 curve if the CFTC clears it in November (a steep backwardation would be the first public forecast of discounting), whether 4Q26 memory contract talks and 2027 HBM4 pricing turn negative, and what ERCOT's December audit says about how much of Texas's 474 GW interconnection queue is phantom demand. The threshold that would flip the call is simple: the H100 index sustained below about $2.00/hr, or spot trading below the one-year contract rate, while Blackwell and Rubin volumes keep arriving; until then compute is being sold at a premium, not a discount, and the risk lives in who is borrowing to build it rather than in the price of the product.

indicators.name: H100 rental price, $/GPU-hour (Silicon Data index; 1-yr contract and spot)
indicators.value: $2.77/hr index (+4.9% 7d) Oct 1 print, up from $2.75 Sep 30, another new high; H200 $3.37 (+2.1% 7d); MI300X $2.63 (+0.4%); H100-hyperscaler $7.20 (+0.3%); RunPod H100 SXM $3.49/$2.69, Lambda $3.99-4.29 (last checked Sep 30); Nebius H100 list +17% live from Oct 1; CME futures launch pushed past Oct 5 (CFTC review to Nov 9)
indicators.why: This is the marginal clearing price of installed AI compute and the most direct public read on whether capacity is being discounted; it is published daily and becomes a CME-listed futures contract on Oct 5, 2026.
indicators.watch: Bearish flip if the Silicon Data H100 index holds below ~$2.00/hr for a month, if spot trades below the one-year contract rate (inversion), or if the CME H100 curve lists in steep (>15%) backwardation; the Oct-2025 trough of $1.70 is the floor to remember.
indicators.note: Oct 1 14:30 UTC: Silicon Data's Oct 1 print is in - SDH100RT $2.77 (+4.9% 7d), 2 cents above Sep 30's $2.75 and the fourth straight daily high. Hopper's other variants held: H200 $3.37 (+2.1% 7d), H100-hyperscaler $7.20 (+0.3%), MI300X $2.63 (+0.4%). Nebius's 17% H100 list rise took effect today. Visibility leg unchanged: the CME/Silicon Data H100 and B200 futures will not list Oct 5 (CFTC review extended to Nov 9), so no public forward curve this quarter. Micron's print is the input-cost echo: DRAM ASP up high-teens QoQ and 2027 HBM contracted at significantly higher prices, so rent keeps rising because the parts do. One demand datapoint from today sits below spot: Tencent is reportedly leasing ~100,000 Nvidia GPUs from Oracle in Southeast Asia for ~$7B over five years (TrendForce via Reuters/FT) - on a straight-line basis that is roughly $14K per GPU per year, about $1.60/GPU-hr at full utilisation, which is what a five-year committed offshore block costs versus $2.77 on-demand. Chip model not disclosed, so treat it as a contract-vs-spot marker, not a like-for-like price.

indicators.name: B200 / Blackwell rental price, $/GPU-hour (on-demand)
indicators.value: Silicon Data B200 $5.86 (+0.2% 7d) Oct 1, up 1.4% on the day from $5.78; B300 $6.78 (-0.3%) unchanged; RunPod B200 $5.98/$6.79, B300 $6.94/$7.89, Lambda B200 $6.69-6.99 (last checked Sep 30); B200/H100 ~2.12x; Nebius B200 +19%, B300 +21% live from Oct 1; CoreWeave running Vera Rubin NVL72 in production (Sep 30)
indicators.why: Blackwell is where new supply lands, so this is the first place a glut would show; if B200 rates fell toward H100 rates while Rubin ships, capacity would be outrunning demand.
indicators.watch: Bearish if tier-1 neocloud B200 on-demand drops below ~$4.50/hr, if the B200/H100 price ratio compresses below ~2x, or if lead times for 8-GPU Blackwell nodes fall to same-week availability.
indicators.note: Oct 1: the B200 index recovered to $5.86 (+0.2% 7d) from Sep 30's $5.78, so Tuesday's dip reversed and the 7-day change flipped back to positive; B300 stayed at $6.78 (-0.3% 7d). With H100 at $2.77 the B200/H100 ratio is ~2.12x - a touch wider than yesterday's 2.10x, still the narrowest band of the quarter and still above the 2x flip line, with B200 far above the $4.50 trigger. Nebius's Blackwell list rises (+19%/+21%) are live today. Rubin is shipping (CoreWeave Vera Rubin NVL72 in production, Cognition first customer) and Blackwell spot did not soften into it, which is the benign version of the watch line. No list-price changes seen at RunPod or Lambda since Sep 30.

indicators.name: Legacy-GPU residual value: used H100 prices, A100/H100 rates and booked useful lives
indicators.value: A100 index $1.58/hr (+0.6% 7d) Oct 1, unchanged, above the $1.50 trigger; A100-hyperscaler $3.76 (+0.3%); used H100 SXM ~$18-27K by age vs $30K list (Jun); Reuters: lenders underwrite GPUs on 3-4 yr schedules vs Nvidia's 'up to a decade', want more than 25% residual guarantees on the $500B financing plan; MSFT/Meta lives unchanged
indicators.why: Depreciation is the biggest cost in a GPU cloud; if old chips still earn money the 5-6 year accounting lives hold and no write-downs are coming, whereas collapsing used-H100 prices would be the first hard evidence of oversupply.
indicators.watch: Bearish if 8-GPU H100 servers trade below ~50% of new-build cost on the secondary market, if A100/H100 rental rates fall below ~$1.50/hr, or if any hyperscaler extends server lives beyond 6 years to flatter earnings; also watch for Hopper impairments at neoclouds.
indicators.note: Oct 1: A100 index flat at $1.58 (+0.6% 7d), A100-hyperscaler $3.76 (+0.3%); H100 $2.77 and H200 $3.37 both firmer, so the rental side of residual value is intact. The new datapoint is on the lender side. Reuters (via BNN Bloomberg, Oct 1) reports Wall Street is pushing back on Nvidia's $500B chip-collateralised financing initiative with Blackstone, Apollo and KKR: Nvidia argues GPUs have a useful life of up to a decade, banks typically underwrite 3-4 year depreciation (Impax's Tony Trzcinka), S&P's Andrew Chang says they run 'well north of five years' but there is not enough history to underwrite long-dated residuals, and lenders want stronger guarantees than the ~25% residual-value floor in some structures plus investment-grade customer backing - CoreWeave's $8.5B A3-rated GPU loan cleared because Meta's contract stood behind it. That is the market saying it will pay for the rental stream, not the chip. No new used-H100 prints, impairments or useful-life changes found.

indicators.name: All-in AI data-center build cost, $ per GW (with GPUs / ex-GPUs)
indicators.value: ~$47B/GW Vera Rubin (≈$32B racks + ≈$15B shell/power/cooling); ~$60B/GW gas-powered campus (Orennia); Project Jupiter $165B for 2.45 GW ≈ $67B/GW all-in; TCS Hyderabad $7.4B for 1 GW ex-GPU shell; CDC Gregadoo (Wagga Wagga) A$15B ≈ US$10B for a 'gigawatt-scale' ex-GPU campus, concept phase
indicators.why: Cost per GW sets the revenue a campus must earn per GPU-hour to clear its cost of capital; rising cost means supply is constrained (good for rental prices) but raises the bar for returns and the size of the debt stack.
indicators.watch: Discounting signal if Nvidia rack ASPs or $/GW start falling (Nvidia gross margin guided below ~72%, rack prices cut) while rental $/hr does not rise; bubble-risk signal if ex-GPU cost (power, shell, turbines) keeps inflating faster than rental rates.
indicators.note: One datapoint added, and it is Australian: Infratil-backed CDC Data Centres is planning a A$15B, gigawatt-scale campus at Gregadoo outside Wagga Wagga (ABC Sep 29; Region Riverina and BeBeez Sep 30). CDC's own site calls it 'concept phase', transmission-level grid connection, closed-loop cooling, no capacity or timeline disclosed. At roughly US$10B for about a GW of shell, power and cooling it sits between TCS Hyderabad (~$7.4B/GW) and the ~$15B/GW US ex-GPU figure - consistent with regional-Australian land and power being cheaper than Texas, not with costs falling. Prior datapoints unchanged: Oracle's Project Jupiter ($165B for 2.45 GW, ~$67B/GW, force majeure Sep 24) and the Orennia $60B/GW gas-campus benchmark. Memory input costs still rising (see memory_prices).

indicators.name: Server DRAM / HBM contract price momentum (QoQ) and DRAM spot
indicators.value: Micron FQ4 (Sep 30): rev $54.23B vs $51.5B est, non-GAAP GM 87.0%, DRAM ASP +high-teens QoQ, NAND ASP ~+30%; FQ1 guide $61.5B ±$1.5B at ~86.25% GM ('low point for FY27'); 'vast majority' of CY2027 HBM bits contracted at significantly higher YoY prices; supply-constrained through 2028; MU -3.1% Thu 10:30 ET on the beat; TrendForce 2027 HBM ASP +121%; DDR5 16Gb spot $57.93 (Oct 1, +0.06%), DDR4 16Gb $83.66 (-0.03%)
indicators.why: Memory is the tightest physical input to AI servers (HBM is 25-30% of a Rubin rack) and contract prices are negotiated quarterly, so this is the earliest cyclical input to turn; a price rollover would precede GPU discounting.
indicators.watch: Bearish when server DRAM or HBM contract prices go negative QoQ, when 2027 HBM4 contracts are signed at lower prices, or when DRAMeXchange DDR5 spot falls >20% from peak; also watch whether CSPs start cutting memory per system (TrendForce now says GPU makers are evaluating 8-Hi instead of 12-Hi HBM stacks), which is the buyers' cost response. Near term: Samsung Q3 prelim Oct 8 (consensus cut to ~107T won); TrendForce 4Q26 contract settlement; Micron's FQ1 print in December against an 86.25% guide it calls the FY27 low.
indicators.note: Thursday's session is the 'sold the news' read: Micron opened lower and was down 3.1% at 10:30 ET from Wednesday's close, after a flat Wednesday and a -0.4% premarket (stockanalysis.com; The Crypto Basic). Targets went up (DA Davidson $2,100, Goldman $1,250), but the tape says an 87% gross margin and a $61.5B guide were already in the price and the 86.25% 'FY27 low' GM guide plus $25B H1 capex were the excuses to take profit. Two product details from the call matter for 2027 pricing: Micron's CTO said HBM4E - both the Nvidia-customised NV-HBM part and the JEDEC part - will move to a foundry process for the base die, unlike in-house HBM4; and a WK Substack report relayed by Wccftech (unverified) says Broadcom's HBM volumes at Samsung are now roughly on par with Nvidia's, eroding Nvidia's volume-discount edge as Broadcom's TPU deployments scale to 5 GW in 2027 and 10 GW in 2028 - more buyers competing for the same stacks, not fewer. DRAM spot, Oct 1 (18:10 Taipei): DDR5 16Gb $57.933 (+0.06%), DDR4 16Gb $83.662 (-0.03%), DDR4 8Gb $46.321 flat, DDR3 4Gb $13.72 flat - a fifth session of sub-0.2% moves, i.e. spot has plateaued at the high while contract keeps stepping up. TrendForce's NAND spot page has not updated since Sep 21 (512Gb TLC wafer $17.50-22.00, -1.0%). Contract-side unchanged: TrendForce 2027 HBM ASP +121% YoY.

indicators.name: Power constraint: ERCOT interconnection queue, gas-turbine backlog and lead times
indicators.value: 474 GW ERCOT queue (~90% data centers); Texas TCEQ permit freeze since Sep 21, compliance report due Oct 19; BNEF: 49.8 GW delayed; GE Vernova 116 GW backlog, ~20 GW/yr output, new orders land ~2030-31; Oracle force majeure on 2.45 GW Project Jupiter (gas pipeline to Feb 2027); US Senate blocks Ratepayer Protection Act 57-43 (Sep 30); Dover DE 18-month and Dixon CA 45-day data-center moratoria
indicators.why: Power, not chips, is now the binding constraint on new capacity, which keeps installed GPUs scarce and rental prices firm; it also reveals how much announced demand is speculative once regulators force projects to prove financing.
indicators.watch: ERCOT files its Batch Zero eligibility-verification and community-impact reports by Dec 10, 2026 for the Dec 17 PUCT open meeting, with RFIs going out Aug-Sep and cure periods Oct-Nov: large queue withdrawals (BNEF flags 49.8 GW at risk) would show phantom demand. Turbine slot cancellations or resales, falling data-center PPA prices, or turbine prices retreating from the $600/kW 2027 forecast would signal the build is slowing. Nearer: TCEQ compliance report Oct 19, Project Jupiter air-permit decision Nov 23.
indicators.note: No new queue, turbine or permit numbers on Oct 1; the Texas freeze stands with TCEQ's report due Oct 19 and ERCOT's audit still targeted for mid-December. The only addition is another local pause: Dixon, California approved a 45-day moratorium on new data-center approvals to study water, power and infrastructure impacts (ABC10, Sep 30), joining Dover, Delaware's 18-month pause - small towns, but the pattern of pre-emptive closures is what turns a queue into phantom demand. What moved Sep 30 was the politics of who pays for power. The US Senate failed 57-43 (60 needed) to advance Sen. Husted's Ratepayer Protection Act, which would have made state regulators decide whether data centers bear the incremental cost of grid build-out; the House had passed it 417-3 on Sep 16, and Democrats blocked it as 'toothless', pushing a GRID Savings Act that would make data centers pay full upgrade costs (KSL/AP, Sep 30). Either version raises the ex-GPU cost of a campus; neither passed, so the status quo holds for now, but both parties are now campaigning on making data centers pay. Prior items unchanged: Oracle's Sep 24 force majeure on Project Jupiter (gas pipeline to Feb 1, 2027, air permit Nov 23); GE Vernova 116 GW backlog against ~20 GW/yr output; Exelon's ~40% cut to 'high-probability' data-center load.

indicators.name: Hyperscaler capex vs cloud backlog (RPO) growth, and capex as % of cloud revenue
indicators.value: Anthropic prospectus: $518B of compute commitments over 7-10 yrs (Broadcom leases $161.2B, Google $111.1B, Amazon $110B, xAI/Nvidia up to $84.5B, Microsoft $31.4B, AMD $20B+), ~80% non-cancelable; Oracle RPO $664B plus reported $7B/5-yr Tencent lease of ~100,000 Nvidia GPUs in SE Asia (~30% upfront), but force majeure on Project Jupiter; Micron: ~$150B RPO, 26 multi-year deals >35% of revenue through 2030, H1 FY27 capex ~$25B; SoftBank $11.1B HY bonds for OpenAI; Goldman: US hyperscaler capex $1.4T in 2027
indicators.why: Capex is the supply side and RPO is the contracted demand side; as long as backlog grows faster than capex the build is pre-sold, but capex above 100% of cloud revenue with negative free cash flow means the cycle is now funded by debt and equity and is sensitive to any demand wobble.
indicators.watch: Bearish if RPO growth decelerates below capex growth for two quarters, if 2027 capex consensus (+57% per Morgan Stanley) gets cut or 'digestion' language appears, or if backlog concentration in a few AI labs (OpenAI, Anthropic) produces a cancellation or renegotiation; Oracle's Project Jupiter force majeure is the first payment-deferral mechanism triggered on a Stargate site - watch whether it spreads.
indicators.note: Oct 1 added a demand-side line to Oracle's ledger from a buyer that cannot buy the chips: Tencent has reportedly signed a ~$7B, five-year deal to lease about 100,000 advanced Nvidia GPUs in Oracle data centers across Southeast Asia, roughly 30% paid upfront (TrendForce, citing Reuters and the FT). US export rules bar Chinese firms from buying the chips but not from renting offshore capacity, so this is export-control arbitrage showing up as cloud RPO - and Tencent's own Q2 capex was already +176% YoY to ~RMB 52.8B with negative free cash flow on AI prepayments. It is also a reminder that part of Oracle's $664B backlog is Chinese demand that Washington could close with a rule change. Supplier-side ledger unchanged from Micron: 26 multi-year agreements >35% of revenue through 2030, ~$150B RPO, vast majority of 2027 HBM bits contracted, H1 FY27 capex ~$25B. Anthropic's $518B of commitments (~80% non-cancelable) stands, with the IPO roadshow still reported for mid-October. Small-neocloud datapoint: GMI Cloud's contracted ARR is >$600M, 9x its end-2025 level, against a $668M raise (see neocloud_credit). The counter-signal remains the financing leg: lenders are now pricing data-center paper as AI credit and pushing back on chip-collateral terms. Next hard data: TSMC Oct 15, then late-October hyperscaler prints.

indicators.name: Neocloud financing: CoreWeave loan/bond spreads, CDS, vendor backstops, customer concentration
indicators.value: CoreWeave $4.2B 2.875% converts (closed Sep 24); Lambda $926M TLB at SOFR+300, Baa2 (Sep 22); CoreWeave loans still ~SOFR+550, debt $35.1B at Jun 30; GMI Cloud $668M = $223M Series B (ARCHIV lead, Nvidia in) + $445M CTBC-led credit facility, ARR >$600M (Oct 1); Reuters: lenders want >25% residual guarantees and IG-customer backing on Nvidia's $500B Blackstone/Apollo/KKR financing plan; data-center ABS $11.9B YTD vs $15.5B in 2025, hyperscaler ABS ~150bp over 5-yr Treasury (+16bp YoY); CleanSpark/Meta $2.23B secured notes ~8.5% with concessions; CRWV $84.88 (-2.6%) 10:30 ET Oct 1, 52-wk $60.55-153.20
indicators.why: Neoclouds are the levered marginal builder of GPU capacity; their cost of debt, covenants and dependence on Nvidia backstops show whether lenders still believe rental prices will cover depreciation, and they are the first place a compute-price decline turns into forced selling.
indicators.watch: Escalation if new deals price above SOFR+600 or 11% yields, CDS above 1,000bp, deals pulled or downsized, Nvidia's rent-back backstop extended to tier-1 neoclouds, or a top customer (CoreWeave's A/B/C are 36%/26%/10% of revenue) renegotiates; improvement if spreads retrace toward the April 9.75% level or if CoreWeave can tap convertible/equity-linked money on Nebius-like terms.
indicators.note: Two Oct 1 datapoints, pulling in opposite directions. Money is still available at the small end: GMI Cloud (Nvidia-backed GPU renter, US/Taiwan/APAC) closed $668M - a $223M Series B led by ARCHIV with Nvidia, DSC, Trend Micro, KB, Kyobo Life and KT, plus a $445M credit facility led by Taiwan's CTBC - against contracted ARR above $600M, 9x end-2025, and ~4 trillion tokens a week (The Next Web). Pricing on the facility was not disclosed, so no spread read. The bigger story is Reuters' survey of lenders on Nvidia's $500B chip-collateralised financing initiative announced in August with Blackstone, Apollo and KKR, which lets AI developers rent Nvidia compute with the chips as collateral and residual-value guarantees as low as 25%: banks say they underwrite GPUs over 3-4 years not Nvidia's 'up to a decade', want stronger guarantees and investment-grade customers behind the cash flows, and point to CoreWeave's $8.5B A3-rated GPU loan as the template because Meta's contract backed it; Wellington's Loren Moran wants 'higher interest rates, bigger financial cushions' (BNN Bloomberg, Oct 1). That is the vendor-finance leg hitting the same wall the ABS leg hit on Sep 30. CRWV fell 2.6% to $84.88 by 10:30 ET Thursday, giving back Wednesday's Vera Rubin bounce, ~45% off the high. Signal stays neutral: equity and bank money still open, but every new structure is being repriced toward the rental contract and away from the chip.

indicators.name: Nvidia data-center revenue growth, gross margin and customer concentration
indicators.value: DC rev $89.0B +117% YoY (Q2 FY27), GM 75.0%, Q3 guide $108B at 74%; one direct customer >=10% (16%); five customers = 70% of receivables; supply commitments $279B; OpenAI Ohio backstop cut to <$120B; $150B buyback added Sep 28 ($235B remaining); $500B chip-collateral financing plan (Blackstone/Apollo/KKR) meeting lender pushback; Tencent reportedly leasing ~100,000 Nvidia GPUs via Oracle SE Asia ($7B/5 yr); Micron: NV-HBM HBM4E to use a foundry base die, 2027 HBM priced 'significantly higher'; NVDA +0.6% 10:30 ET Oct 1
indicators.why: Nvidia's margin is the purest read on whether GPUs are being discounted at the source, and its concentration plus growing vendor-financing (backstops, campus guarantees) shows how much of demand is circular.
indicators.watch: Bearish if gross margin is guided below ~72% for more than one quarter, data-center revenue grows <5% sequentially, three-customer concentration exceeds 60% in the 10-Q, DSO climbs past 60 days, or backstop commitments expand beyond the $108.5B disclosed; Q3 FY27 report due ~Nov 2026.
indicators.note: Operating figures unchanged from the Aug 26 10-Q and the Sep 28 buyback; NVDA was +0.6% at 10:30 ET Thursday, near its high, while Micron sold off. Three Oct 1 read-throughs. Demand: Tencent's reported $7B, five-year lease of ~100,000 Nvidia GPUs in Oracle's Southeast Asian data centers (TrendForce via Reuters/FT) is China demand reaching Nvidia silicon through a cloud lease that current export rules allow - incremental volume, but a line Washington could cut. Financing: Reuters finds lenders resisting the terms of Nvidia's $500B chip-collateralised financing plan (3-4 year underwriting vs 'up to a decade', want >25% residual guarantees and IG customers), so the vendor-finance channel that would let Nvidia pull demand forward is getting more expensive, not cheaper - the circularity line in the 'why' is being tested by the people who have to fund it. Cost: Micron's CTO said HBM4E, including the Nvidia-customised NV-HBM, moves its base die to a foundry process, and a secondary report (WK Substack via Wccftech, unverified) says Broadcom's Samsung HBM volumes are now on par with Nvidia's, ending Nvidia's volume-discount edge as TPU deployments scale to 5 GW in 2027. With 2027 HBM already contracted 'significantly higher', the 74% Q3 guide has to absorb dearer memory without a bigger buyer's discount. Rubin revenue is live (CoreWeave Vera Rubin NVL72 in production). The public forward curve remains off the table (CFTC review to Nov 9). Next data: Q3 FY27 print ~Nov.
